summary_responses.response: The National Park Service issued a final rule amending Mammoth Cave National Park's special regulations to designate about 37 miles of multi-use trails for bicycle use and to allow horseback riding on the 5.4-mile Houchin Ferry North/Ollie Road, effective December 21, 2026. This action implements the preferred alternative identified in the park's Comprehensive Land and River Trails Plan and Environmental Assessment, which was supported by a Finding of No Significant Impact signed in December 2024. Final trail alignments will be determined within a 60-foot corridor and may be adjusted on the ground to avoid sensitive resources, with public notification through the superintendent's compendium and park maps; electric bicycles may be allowed on trails open to traditional bicycles at the discretion of the superintendent under 36 CFR 4.30. The NPS notes the Houchin Ferry North/Ollie Road will be open to equestrian use under the new regulations, and all management actions will be conducted to protect natural and cultural resources while expanding visitor access.
